environment: Disposable isolated PostgreSQL; labelled fixtures, Auth stand-ins and stubbed generation; no hosted data or provider calls

checks.name: Forward migration applies to the complete current chain without rewriting existing trip/member/invite rows
Only five authorised old bodies change; every existing ACL/search path and other function body is preserved
Anonymous caller cannot invoke organiser editing
Unverified account cannot edit
New invitations use random UUIDs while existing 64-hex invitations remain valid
Destination availability overlaps directly, zero reserve is accepted, and non-test-prefix real journeys can opt in to Gemini
New destination protocol rejects hidden travel buffers
Negative allowance remains rejected
Gemini admission allows an ordinary trip name and sends only reviewed shared context; generation remains a local stub
Member/outsider cannot obtain host edit access: member
Member/outsider cannot obtain host edit access: outsider
Stale source plan cannot be edited
Stale organiser edits return the complete HTTP409 conflict envelope without database retry semantics
Host cannot create gaps or overlaps
Host cannot exceed another traveller’s private ceiling
Host master edit creates one idempotent immutable draft, keeps original requests and discloses displaced must-haves, and requires fresh reviews
Editing a locked plan preserves its immutable lock, previous reviews and document
An ordinary member cannot lock the edited master plan
Host editing exposes no other traveller’s private origin, budget or raw requirement text
Host edits keep the affected author’s unresolved must-have check instead of overriding it
Name-only host edits preserve confirmed inputs and the current draft
Members cannot edit trip details
Trip edit cannot replace a date option with another trip identifier
Material trip edits pause the current plan, require fresh confirmations and preserve every historical version
Interpreter still requires explicit consent
Owner-only interpreter has no TEST name/text gate; consent, revision, digest and receipts still apply
New public wrapper is invoker-only and callable only by authenticated users
